title: Non-Similar Paths
statementMd:
*After years of research, you (Nick Belov) finally find your favorite biking place. You want to explore as many different bike paths as possible. However, you don't see a difference in exploring two bike paths that are very similar. You want to know how many bike paths you can explore such that each path is non-similar to any of your previously explored paths. *

You are given an n×m𝑛×𝑚 grid. Each cell is either **passable** or **impassable**.

A **valid path** starts at the top-left cell (1,1)(1,1) and ends at the bottom-right cell (n,m). At each step, you may move either **right** or **down**, and every cell visited by the path must be passable.

Represent each valid path by a string containing m−1 characters 'R' and n−1 characters 'D', denoting moves right and down, respectively.

Two valid paths a and b are called **similar** if there exists a sequence of valid paths a=q1,q2,…,q|q|=b such that, for every 1≤j<|q|, the paths qj and qj+1 differ in exactly 2 adjacent positions.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/dc05613cc00e4fb5d611943af640e0407c59d8e5.png)

Let S be a set of valid paths such that no two distinct paths in S are similar.

Find the maximum possible size of S. Since the answer may be large, output it modulo 998244353.

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t (1≤t≤105). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains two integers n and m (1≤n,m≤106,2≤n⋅m≤106) — the number of rows and columns of the grid.

Each of the next n lines contains a string of length m describing one row of the grid.

A '.' denotes a passable cell, and a '#' denotes an impassable cell.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n⋅m over all test cases does not exceed 106.

## Output

For each test case, output one integer — the maximum possible size of S, modulo 998244353.

## Note

In the first test case (same as second picture), here is a possible set S:

{RRRRDDDD,DDDDRRRR}

In the second test case, the starting cell is impassable so there are no valid paths.

In the third and fourth test cases there is only 1 valid path.
